content.title: Delayed-Turn Horror | Silhouette Contamination and Lens Breach
content.summary: An adult archivist turns once as ink grows from collar to arch, then covers the lens with a brass key hand. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One clearly adult identity, one fixed frontal corridor and one back-facing baseline precede all threat cues. + Exactly one complete turn establishes the face before silhouette contamination begins. + The anomalous material grows in continuous registered stages while architecture remains unchanged. + Expression and outline escalate without face replacement, body mutation or geographic reset. + Only one terminal lens breach follows a restrained hold and ends on visible contact.
quick_start.recommended_input: Lock one clearly adult original night archivist with a blunt black bob, ash-blue coat and brass key at the far end of a narrow cream records corridor; she begins facing away from a fixed frontal camera. A matte ink fringe grows from the coat collar in three visible stages—shoulder line, jaw line, then overhead arch—while every shelf and ceiling lamp stays fixed. She holds for one beat, then takes a single rapid three-step approach and covers the lens with the brass key hand; cut only on full contact.

Exactly one complete turn establishes the face before silhouette contamination begins.
Expression and outline escalate without face replacement, body mutation or geographic reset.
Only one terminal lens breach follows a restrained hold and ends on visible contact.
